title: KPT in verbs
focus: Use familiar strong-to-weak KPT changes in short, complete A1 minä sentences; every non-target sentence part is supplied.

exercises.prompt: Complete “I sleep well.” Minä ____ hyvin. Use nukkua (“to sleep”), supplied stem nukku-, and the minä ending -n; hyvin means “well”.
exercises.explanation: Minä nukun hyvin means “I sleep well”. Change kk to k in the supplied stem nukku- to make nuku-, then add the minä ending -n: nukun. Minä and hyvin stay unchanged.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: Subject (who) + verb (action or state) + manner word

parts.role: Subject — names who sleeps.
parts.formation: minä is the basic pronoun meaning “I”; it is supplied unchanged.

parts.role: Verb — tells what I do.
parts.formation: Use the supplied stem nukku-. Change kk to k to make nuku-, then add the minä ending -n: nukun.

parts.role: Manner word — tells how I sleep.
parts.formation: hyvin is supplied as a complete fixed word meaning “well”. No ending rule is being tested.

exercises.prompt: Choose “I am waiting here.” Use odottaa (“to wait”), supplied stem odotta-, and täällä (“here”).
exercises.explanation: Minä odotan täällä means “I am waiting here”. Change tt to t in the supplied stem odotta- to make odota-, then add the minä ending -n: odotan.

Correct. Change tt to t in odotta- to make odota-, then add -n: odotan.
“Odottan” keeps the strong tt. Change tt to t before the minä ending: odota- + n = odotan.
Odottaa is the dictionary form “to wait”. The sentence needs the minä form odota- + n = odotan.

exercises.instruction: Translate the complete sentence into English.
exercises.explanation: Minä saavun tänään can mean “I am arriving today”, “I arrive today” or “I will arrive today”. Finnish normally uses the present tense for a future event when a time word such as tänään makes the timing clear. The dictionary form is saapua. Its stem is saapu-. Change p to v to make saavu-, then add the minä ending -n: saavun.
